name: FUN_BC_CONNECTIONS
description: This table stores blockchain connection information.

columns.name: CONNECTION_ID
columns.description: Identifier of the connection and it is the primary key.

columns.name: CONNECTION_NAME
columns.description: Name of the connection and it should be unique for each application

columns.name: CONNECTION_DESCRIPTION
columns.description: The description of the connection.

columns.name: CONNECTION_TYPE_ID
columns.description: Identifier of the connection type.

columns.name: ENDPOINT_URL
columns.description: The endpoint url of the connection.

columns.name: ALTERNATIVE_ENDPOINT_URL
columns.description: The alternative  endpoint url of the connection.

columns.name: USER_NAME
columns.description: The user name to trigger the blockchain service.

columns.name: USER_KEY
columns.description: The key of the user name, the user's password which is encrypted and stored in weblogic sever can be decrypted with this key.

columns.name: IDENTITY_SERVICE_URL
columns.description: The REST server portion of the Oracle Identity Cloud Service Instance URL.

columns.name: CLIENT_ID
columns.description: The client ID of  the application in  Oracle Blockchain service. The client ID can be copied from  the console of Oracle Blockchain service and will be used to fetch access token.

columns.name: CLIENT_SECRET
columns.description: The client secret of the application in  Oracle Blockchain service.The client secret can be copied from  the console of Oracle Blockchain service and will be used to fetch access token.

columns.name: PRIMARY_AUDIENCE_URL
columns.description: The primary audience URL of the application in  Oracle Blockchain service.

columns.name: ALLOWED_SCOPE_CODE
columns.description: The 1PaaS permission scope of the application in  Oracle Blockchain service.

columns.name: ACCESS_TOKEN
columns.description: The access token fetched from Oracle Identity Cloud Service will be used during triggering blockchain service.

columns.name: REFRESH_TOKEN
columns.description: This refresh token fetched from Oracle Identity Cloud Service will be used to refresh the access token.

columns.name: ACTIVE_FLAG
columns.description: Indicates whether the connection is used in the related application.

columns.name: CHANNEL_NAME
columns.description: Channel name configured in blockchain network.

columns.name: CHAINCODE_NAME
columns.description: Chaincode name deployed under the channel.

columns.name: CHAINCODE_VERSION
columns.description: Chaincode version of the deployed chaincode.

columns.name: APPLICATION_ID
columns.description: Unique application identification number.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.
